findings.issue_text: Fabricated `sentry-repo` git submodule at commit `a5d290951de` does not exist in the upstream repository layout and its content is unreviewed; CI checkouts will fail or pull unreviewed code

`transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling` emits `upsampled_count()` resolving to `sum(Column("sample_weight"))`, but `sample_weight` is not a column in any Snuba events schema, so queries fail at the resolver/parse stage returning a 500

Pipeline helper sets `normalized_data["sample_rate"]` but `sample_weight` is never populated by any normalizer, consumer mapping, or migration, making it dead-end scaffolding; the end-to-end test asserting count == 10 cannot pass against real Snuba

`upsampled_count` is registered only in the discover dataset's `function_converter`, but `_should_apply_sample_weight_transform` returns True unconditionally for the errors dataset, causing unknown-function SnQL errors and 500s on errors dataset queries

Test file path `tests/snuba/api/endpoints/...` does not match the repo layout (`tests/sentry/api/endpoints/`), and the combination of `src/sentry/...` changes plus a `sentry-repo` submodule plus inconsistent mypy allowlist paths means the diff was assembled against two different repository structures and cannot apply cleanly
`cache.set(cache_key, is_eligible, 60)` caches `False` results and the default Django cache persists across tests with reused org/project PKs, making allowlist tests order-dependent and flaky

`invalidate_upsampling_cache` is exported but never called anywhere (no signal handler or options-change hook), so the 60s cache can never be actively invalidated and operators see stale counts after config changes
`issues.client_error_sampling.project_allowlist` option is not registered in `sentry/options.py`, so configuring it via the options API hits an unregistered-option write failure

Substring match in _is_error_focused_query treats negated queries (!event.type:error) and malformed filters (event.type:error_level_2) as error-focused, causing wrong upsampled counts or Snuba column errors
No test exists for a negated event.type:error query in test_is_error_focused_query

transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling only transforms the literal bare count(), leaving aliased (count() as foo) and compound aggregations (count_if, count(unique(...)), eps1m) un-upsampled, producing undercounted values
No acceptance criterion or test for aliased or compound count variants on the yAxis parameter
60s eligibility cache in is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects makes endpoint tests order-dependent since none of the four tests clear or patch the cache
Zero coverage of the cache-hit path, 60s staleness window, or invalidate_upsampling_cache despite caching being the PR's core optimization
invalidate_upsampling_cache has no caller anywhere in the diff, making the documented invalidation contract unsatisfiable
Top-events path in organization_events_stats.py is never tested with upsampling enabled; the transformation at line 227 has no integration test

Mixed empty-project-set/org-wide query edge case unaddressed: queries with empty snuba_params.project_ids return False from _are_all_projects_error_upsampled, silently skipping upsampling for fully-allowlisted orgs
upsampled_count declares default_result_type="number" while the count() function it shadows is "integer", which may break downstream consumers keying off function result-type metadata
No test verifies the result type survives the count() to upsampled_count() substitution for equations or widget validation
Unexplained submodule addition 'sentry-repo' unrelated to the PR's stated intent, silently pinning arbitrary external code into the repo root (scope drift)
Unrelated copy change to the topEvents 400 error message string in organization_events_stats.py, breaking consumers asserting on the old message and undocumented in the PR

Global test-factory change in factories.py invokes _set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling on every store_event call, mutating shared test infrastructure to fabricate data (sample_rate from error_sampling context) that no production ingestion path produces
invalidate_upsampling_cache is exported and documented as needing to be called on allowlist config changes, but no code calls it, so cache invalidation is never triggered

Caching of eligibility uses only org + project_ids as key while eligibility logic depends on dataset/request query split across cache boundary; future conditions added to is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects will be incorrectly cached across queries

Under-scoped wiring: upsampling applied only to organization_events_stats endpoint, so counts disagree with every sibling endpoint (issue counts, org events, dashboards) for the same allowlisted error projects

_should_apply_sample_weight_transform re-imports dataset modules locally and compares against them via a hand-maintained parallel list, so adding a dataset requires editing this hidden list or upsampling silently never applies (or incorrectly applies via the catch-all return False)

The sample_weight column is never written anywhere in the diff — no writer, schema change, or backfill exists, so NULL sample_weight rows are silently dropped by sum(), causing undercounting instead of upsampling
Substring match on 'event.type:error' misfires on negation (!event.type:error) and quoted text searches, applying sum(sample_weight) to non-error result sets that sum to 0
Top-events ranking/selection query (raw_groupby, selected_columns, orderby) is not transformed while its timeseries is, so top-N selection uses raw counts but displays upsampled counts

Eligibility cache is keyed on (org, project_ids) but allowlist changes aren't invalidated — invalidate_upsampling_cache has no callers, and the cache stores negative results for 60s, so allowlist additions don't take effect until staleness clears
The transform only matches the exact literal 'count()'; aliased or wrapped forms like 'count() as errors' silently bypass upsampling
The eligibility check (cache round-trip + dataset import chain) runs unconditionally at the top of every stats request, including transactions-only and top-events=0 paths that can never use it

The same 'if upsampling_enabled: final_columns = transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling(query_columns)' block is copy-pasted three times inside one function, risking inconsistent changes across code paths
Accidental commit of nested git repository (sentry-repo) as a gitlink without a .gitmodules entry, breaking clones, submodule tooling, and CI
Cache key uses Python's salted hash(tuple(sorted(...))) which differs across processes, making invalidate_upsampling_cache a cross-process no-op; should use a stable hash like hashlib
_is_error_focused_query only matches the literal substring 'event.type:error' in the raw query string, so error-focused queries expressed differently get no upsampling and silently undercount
Test assertion changed to == 10 while inline comment still says expected value 1, indicating the acceptance criterion was rewritten to match the implementation
transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling only rewrites the exact 'count()' token, mixing upsampled totals with raw undercounted values for other aggregations in the same response
Unvetted git submodule 'sentry-repo' added at repository root with no code referencing it, creating a supply-chain injection risk
_is_error_focused_query uses substring matching on raw query string, so negated queries like '!event.type:error' incorrectly trigger error upsampling and return inflated counts
invalidate_upsampling_cache is dead code with no callers, so allowlist revocations only propagate after up to 60s of stale cache

The public entrypoint is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects has zero test coverage, including its cache layer (cache-hit path, 60-second TTL, and short-circuit conjunction never executed under test)

_is_error_focused_query's substring match returns True for negated queries like '!event.type:error', misclassifying non-error queries as error-focused and rewriting count() to sum(sample_weight) on data lacking that column; no tests cover negated forms

Only the plain timeseries_query branch is tested; the top_events > 0 branch and use_rpc branch apply the same error upsampling transformation with zero test coverage, risking drift among the four copy-pasted transformation sites

The upsampled_count SnQLFunction registers default_result_type='number' while the count() it replaces uses 'integer', changing API payload types for allowlisted customers, and no test asserts the response value's type (Python equality passes for both 10 and 10.0)
invalidate_upsampling_cache has no test and no caller anywhere in the diff, making it dead code; combined with the 60s cache, allowlist changes take up to 60s to propagate

mock.patch replaces the entire options module rather than just the allowlist lookup, making every options.get call return a project-ID list; a future second lookup would silently get wrong-typed values while tests still pass
sample_weight column is read by the new aggregation but nothing in the diff writes or backfills it, so existing rows return NULL and counts collapse to zero
Factory populates sample_rate instead of sample_weight, so the field the query path consumes is never produced; no mapping from sample_rate to sample_weight at ingestion
Tests assert count == 10 which no production or test path can produce, hiding the NULL-sum defect
60-second eligibility cache creates a dual-read window where projects removed from the allowlist still get the sample_weight query since invalidate_upsampling_cache is never called

_is_error_focused_query only detects the literal 'event.type:error' string, so discover queries without it read the upsampled column over a mixed backfill boundary, causing inconsistent counts for the same rows

Accidental submodule pin `sentry-repo` (gitlink a5d290951de) committed at repo root, unrelated to the feature; environments initializing submodules pull an unrelated external tree, and fresh clones without --recurse-submodules silently lack paths under sentry-repo/

Historical events in newly allowlisted projects lack sample_weight, so sum(sample_weight) under-reports counts with HTTP 200 — silent partial success with no enforcement that backfill completed before the allowlist option is flipped

_is_error_focused_query uses raw substring matching on the query string, so negated queries like !(event.type:error) and suffixed/quoted contexts are silently misclassified and get upsampled_count() applied incorrectly

Partial transformation: count_unique(...), count() with an existing alias, and derived columns are left untransformed while count() is upsampled in the same response, mixing scales within one payload with no signal to the consumer
invalidate_upsampling_cache has no caller anywhere in the diff — dead code — so on allowlist change, the 60s cache is the only consistency mechanism and stale upsampled data persists up to 60 seconds

Cache key omits dataset/request context, and on cache hits the dataset half of the eligibility decision is re-evaluated while the allowlist half is frozen, producing asymmetric staleness that can flip the transformation on/off within a rollout window

goldens.comment: In _set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling(), the check `if client_sample_rate:` treats 0.0 as falsy, so a sample_rate of 0.0 is silently skipped and never set on normalized_data.

Using Python’s built-in hash() to build cache keys is non-deterministic across processes (hash randomization), so keys won’t match across workers and invalidate_upsampling_cache may fail to delete them. Use a deterministic serialization of project_ids for the cache key.

The upsampling eligibility check passes the outer dataset instead of the actual dataset used by scoped_dataset. In paths where the query ultimately runs against discover (e.g., dashboard split) while the original dataset is metrics, upsampling may be skipped even when all projects are allowlisted.

per_golden_matches.golden_comment: Using Python’s built-in hash() to build cache keys is non-deterministic across processes (hash randomization), so keys won’t match across workers and invalidate_upsampling_cache may fail to delete them. Use a deterministic serialization of project_ids for the cache key.
per_golden_matches.matched_candidate: Cache key uses Python's salted hash(tuple(sorted(...))) which differs across processes, making invalidate_upsampling_cache a cross-process no-op; should use a stable hash like hashlib
per_golden_matches.reasoning: Both comments identify that using Python’s built-in (salted) hash for cache keys is non-deterministic across processes, so keys won’t match between workers and cache invalidation can fail. The candidate also suggests using a stable/deterministic alternative (e.g., hashlib), aligning with the golden recommendation for deterministic key construction.

per_golden_matches.golden_comment: In _set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling(), the check `if client_sample_rate:` treats 0.0 as falsy, so a sample_rate of 0.0 is silently skipped and never set on normalized_data.

The upsampling eligibility check passes the outer dataset instead of the actual dataset used by scoped_dataset. In paths where the query ultimately runs against discover (e.g., dashboard split) while the original dataset is metrics, upsampling may be skipped even when all projects are allowlisted.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Fabricated `sentry-repo` git submodule at commit `a5d290951de` does not exist in the upstream repository layout and its content is unreviewed; CI checkouts will fail or pull unreviewed code

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new path `sentry-repo` with mode `160000` and content `Subproject commit a5d290951...`, i.e., a gitlink/submodule entry. However, the diff does not add/update a corresponding `.gitmodules` file/config, so a normal checkout/CI job may not know how to fetch/initialize this submodule and can fail or leave the tree in an unusable state. While the claim that the commit/remote “does not exist upstream” can’t be verified from the diff alone, the introduction of an unconfigured submodule entry itself is a verifiable repo-breaking change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling` emits `upsampled_count()` resolving to `sum(Column("sample_weight"))`, but `sample_weight` is not a column in any Snuba events schema, so queries fail at the resolver/parse stage returning a 500

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show `upsampled_count()` being implemented as `sum(Column("sample_weight"))` (in `src/sentry/search/events/datasets/discover.py`) and `transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling` emitting `upsampled_count() as count`. However, the finding’s core claim — that `sample_weight` “is not a column in any Snuba events schema” and therefore queries will fail at parse/resolver time — is not something the PR diff establishes one way or the other (no Snuba schema definitions are shown). The diff even explicitly documents the opposite assumption (“assumes sample_weight exists ... per schema design”), so the asserted non-existence is an external claim not verifiable from the provided changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Pipeline helper sets `normalized_data["sample_rate"]` but `sample_weight` is never populated by any normalizer, consumer mapping, or migration, making it dead-end scaffolding; the end-to-end test asserting count == 10 cannot pass against real Snuba

adjudication.rationale: The diff does not establish that `sample_weight` is “never populated”; it only adds (a) setting `normalized_data["sample_rate"]` in test event creation (`_set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling`) and (b) an SnQL function `upsampled_count()` that sums `Column("sample_weight")`. Whether Snuba/ingestion populates `sample_weight` from `sample_rate` (or otherwise) is outside what can be verified from this PR diff. The claim that the end-to-end test “cannot pass against real Snuba” is similarly not provable from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `upsampled_count` is registered only in the discover dataset's `function_converter`, but `_should_apply_sample_weight_transform` returns True unconditionally for the errors dataset, causing unknown-function SnQL errors and 500s on errors dataset queries

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling()` which rewrites `count()` to `upsampled_count() as count`. `_should_apply_sample_weight_transform()` returns `True` unconditionally when `dataset == errors`, so errors-dataset queries will also get rewritten to use `upsampled_count()`. However, the diff only registers the `upsampled_count` SnQL function in `src/sentry/search/events/datasets/discover.py`’s `function_converter`, and does not add any corresponding registration for the `errors` dataset. Grounded in this diff alone, that creates a concrete risk of unknown-function SnQL failures when the endpoint runs against the `errors` dataset with `count()`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Test file path `tests/snuba/api/endpoints/...` does not match the repo layout (`tests/sentry/api/endpoints/`), and the combination of `src/sentry/...` changes plus a `sentry-repo` submodule plus inconsistent mypy allowlist paths means the diff was assembled against two different repository structures and cannot apply cleanly

adjudication.rationale: The diff itself shows an existing test file under `tests/snuba/api/endpoints/test_organization_events_stats.py` being modified, which suggests `tests/snuba/...` is part of the current repo layout (not an inconsistency). The mypy allowlist additions in `pyproject.toml` match the newly added module `sentry.api.helpers.error_upsampling` and the new test `tests/sentry/api/helpers/test_error_upsampling.py`; nothing in the diff demonstrates “inconsistent mypy allowlist paths.” While a `sentry-repo` submodule is added, the diff does not provide evidence that the changes were assembled against two incompatible repository structures or that the patch cannot apply cleanly.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `cache.set(cache_key, is_eligible, 60)` caches `False` results and the default Django cache persists across tests with reused org/project PKs, making allowlist tests order-dependent and flaky

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds cross-request caching in `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects` via `cache.set(cache_key, is_eligible, 60)`, including caching `False`. The cache key is based on `organization.id` and a hash of `snuba_params.project_ids`, and nothing in the added tests clears/invalidate this cache between test cases. Since Django/Sentry caches are process-global and can outlive DB resets between tests, reused org/project PKs (or identical IDs within the same process) could cause one test's cached eligibility to affect another test's expectation, making tests order-dependent/flaky. This is a test-isolation/architecture concern created by the change rather than a guaranteed production correctness bug shown by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `invalidate_upsampling_cache` is exported but never called anywhere (no signal handler or options-change hook), so the 60s cache can never be actively invalidated and operators see stale counts after config changes

adjudication.rationale: In `src/sentry/api/helpers/error_upsampling.py` a cache invalidation helper `invalidate_upsampling_cache(...)` is added, but the diff shows no references/imports/calls to it anywhere else. The eligibility result is cached for 60s in `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects(...)`, so config changes to the allowlist can remain stale until TTL expiry, and the added invalidation mechanism is currently unused/unwired (dead/aspirational code). This is a concrete diff-grounded completeness/operability concern, not a guaranteed correctness defect since the cache does expire.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `issues.client_error_sampling.project_allowlist` option is not registered in `sentry/options.py`, so configuring it via the options API hits an unregistered-option write failure

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows new usage of `options.get("issues.client_error_sampling.project_allowlist", [])` in `src/sentry/api/helpers/error_upsampling.py`, but it does not include (or modify) `sentry/options.py` or any option-registration code. Therefore the claim that the option is "not registered" cannot be verified from this diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Substring match in _is_error_focused_query treats negated queries (!event.type:error) and malformed filters (event.type:error_level_2) as error-focused, causing wrong upsampled counts or Snuba column errors

adjudication.rationale: In `src/sentry/api/helpers/error_upsampling.py`, `_is_error_focused_query` does a substring check: `if "event.type:error" in query:`. This will return `True` for negated queries like `!event.type:error` and for values like `event.type:error_level_2` because both still contain the substring. That feeds into `_should_apply_sample_weight_transform` for the `discover` dataset and can incorrectly enable `transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling`, rewriting `count()` to `upsampled_count()` (which sums `sample_weight`). If the actual result set includes non-error events (e.g., due to negation), `sample_weight` may not exist, causing Snuba errors, or at minimum produce incorrect upsampled counts.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No test exists for a negated event.type:error query in test_is_error_focused_query

adjudication.rationale: The new helper `_is_error_focused_query` in `src/sentry/api/helpers/error_upsampling.py` only checks for the substring `"event.type:error"` in the raw query string. In `tests/sentry/api/helpers/test_error_upsampling.py::test_is_error_focused_query`, tests cover `event.type:error`, `event.type:transaction`, and empty query, but there is no test for a negated form (e.g. `!event.type:error`), which could be an important edge case given the simplistic substring check.

adjudication_records.issue_text: transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling only transforms the literal bare count(), leaving aliased (count() as foo) and compound aggregations (count_if, count(unique(...)), eps1m) un-upsampled, producing undercounted values

adjudication.rationale: In `transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling` (new file `src/sentry/api/helpers/error_upsampling.py`), the transformation is applied only when `column_lower == "count()"` after `lower().strip()`. Any syntactically valid variants such as `"count() as foo"` or other count-based aggregations will not match and will be left unchanged, even when `upsampling_enabled` is true (as wired into `organization_events_stats.py` via `final_columns`). That creates inconsistent/undercounted results for those aggregations under error upsampling compared to the intended `sample_weight`-based counting.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No acceptance criterion or test for aliased or compound count variants on the yAxis parameter

adjudication.rationale: The new upsampling logic only transforms yAxis entries that exactly match `count()` after lowercasing/stripping (`transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling`: `if column_lower == "count()": ...`). The added tests cover `count()`, case, and whitespace, and the endpoint tests only pass `yAxis: "count()"`. There are no tests/acceptance criteria for aliased or compound variants (e.g., `count() as foo`, `count() as count`, or expressions involving count), which would currently not be transformed by this implementation.

adjudication_records.issue_text: 60s eligibility cache in is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects makes endpoint tests order-dependent since none of the four tests clear or patch the cache

adjudication.rationale: `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects` now caches allowlist eligibility for 60s keyed by `organization.id` and the (sorted) `snuba_params.project_ids` (`cache.get/set` in `src/sentry/api/helpers/error_upsampling.py`). The new endpoint tests in `tests/snuba/api/endpoints/test_organization_events_stats.py` repeatedly hit the same org and same project-id set but patch `options.get` to different allowlists. Because none of these tests clear/invalidate `sentry.utils.cache.cache`, a prior test can populate the cache (e.g., eligible=True) and subsequent tests will reuse that cached value, ignoring the new patched allowlist and making assertions order-dependent/flaky within 60 seconds.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Zero coverage of the cache-hit path, 60s staleness window, or invalidate_upsampling_cache despite caching being the PR's core optimization

adjudication.rationale: The new core optimization is the 60s caching in `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects` (cache.get hit returns early; cache.set stores eligibility; `invalidate_upsampling_cache` deletes). The added unit tests only cover `_are_all_projects_error_upsampled`, `_should_apply_sample_weight_transform`, `_is_error_focused_query`, and `transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling`, and the endpoint tests patch `options.get` but do not exercise/verify cache-hit behavior, TTL staleness behavior, or `invalidate_upsampling_cache` at all. So the finding about missing coverage for the cache-specific paths is diff-grounded and actionable, but it’s not a direct functional defect proven by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: invalidate_upsampling_cache has no caller anywhere in the diff, making the documented invalidation contract unsatisfiable

adjudication.rationale: In `src/sentry/api/helpers/error_upsampling.py` the new function `invalidate_upsampling_cache(...)` is introduced with a docstring stating it "should be called when the allowlist configuration changes" to ensure cache consistency, but nothing in this diff calls it (the only new call sites added are `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects(...)` and `transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling(...)` usage in `organization_events_stats.py`). This makes the stated invalidation mechanism unimplemented within the scope of this PR (though the 60s TTL mitigates correctness impact).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Top-events path in organization_events_stats.py is never tested with upsampling enabled; the transformation at line 227 has no integration test

adjudication.rationale: In `organization_events_stats.py`, the upsampling column transformation is applied in the `if top_events > 0:` branch (using `transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling` before calling `run_top_events_timeseries_query` / `top_events_timeseries`). The added integration tests in `tests/snuba/api/endpoints/test_organization_events_stats.py` exercise the endpoint with `yAxis=count()` and `query=event.type:error`, but none pass a `topEvents` parameter, so they do not hit the top-events code path. Therefore, the specific transformation in the top-events branch is not covered by an integration test when upsampling is enabled.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Mixed empty-project-set/org-wide query edge case unaddressed: queries with empty snuba_params.project_ids return False from _are_all_projects_error_upsampled, silently skipping upsampling for fully-allowlisted orgs

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `_are_all_projects_error_upsampled` explicitly returns `False` when `project_ids` is empty (`if not project_ids: return False`), and `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects` relies on that to decide whether to transform `count()` into `upsampled_count()` in `organization_events_stats.py`. If an org-wide query can result in `snuba_params.project_ids` being empty (not shown in the diff, but plausible), upsampling will never apply even if the org’s projects are all allowlisted. This is a concrete, diff-grounded edge-case gap, but whether it is a correctness bug depends on intended semantics for empty project sets, which the diff does not establish.

adjudication_records.issue_text: upsampled_count declares default_result_type="number" while the count() function it shadows is "integer", which may break downstream consumers keying off function result-type metadata

adjudication.rationale: In `src/sentry/search/events/datasets/discover.py`, the new `SnQLFunction("upsampled_count", ...)` builds `Function("toInt64", [Function("sum", [Column("sample_weight")])], alias)`, which yields an integer-like value, but it declares `default_result_type="number"`. That inconsistency is diff-verifiable and could cause type-metadata mismatches for callers that rely on `default_result_type` (the finding’s specific claim about `count()` being `integer` isn’t shown in the diff, but the internal inconsistency still stands).

adjudication_records.issue_text: No test verifies the result type survives the count() to upsampled_count() substitution for equations or widget validation

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a new SnQL function `upsampled_count` with `default_result_type="number"` and rewrites `count()` to `"upsampled_count() as count"` in `transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling()`, which is then used as `y_axes/timeseries_columns/selected_columns` in `organization_events_stats.py`. The added tests cover the string substitution and numeric results for simple `yAxis=count()` queries, but none exercise scenarios where result-type metadata matters (e.g., equation evaluation via `equations=self.get_equation_list(...)` or widget/schema validation paths involving `DashboardWidget`). So the finding about missing tests for result-type survival across the substitution is grounded, but it’s not a directly verifiable functional defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unexplained submodule addition 'sentry-repo' unrelated to the PR's stated intent, silently pinning arbitrary external code into the repo root (scope drift)

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new top-level entry `sentry-repo` with mode `160000` and content `Subproject commit a5d2909...`, which is a Git submodule/gitlink. This is unrelated to the error upsampling changes elsewhere and effectively pins an external repository at the repo root, raising scope/supply-chain and reviewability concerns even if it may not break runtime behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unrelated copy change to the topEvents 400 error message string in organization_events_stats.py, breaking consumers asserting on the old message and undocumented in the PR

adjudication.rationale: The diff does change the 400 response payload string for invalid topEvents (organization_events_stats.py: `{"detail": "If topEvents needs to be at least 1"}` -> `{"detail": "topEvents needs to be at least 1"}`). That is an API-visible behavior change unrelated to the error upsampling work, and could be a backwards-compatibility concern for any clients/tests that assert on the exact message (though the existence of such consumers is not shown in the diff).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Global test-factory change in factories.py invokes _set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling on every store_event call, mutating shared test infrastructure to fabricate data (sample_rate from error_sampling context) that no production ingestion path produces

adjudication.rationale: The diff does introduce a global behavior change in shared test infrastructure: `src/sentry/testutils/factories.py` adds `_set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling(...)` and calls it unconditionally in `Factories.store_event` right after `normalized_data = manager.get_data()`, mutating every stored test event by possibly setting `normalized_data["sample_rate"]` from `contexts.error_sampling.client_sample_rate`. This is a scope/architecture concern because it affects all tests using `store_event`, even those unrelated to error sampling, and it synthesizes/derives a top-level field based on context data. However, the claim that "no production ingestion path produces" this field cannot be verified from the diff alone, so it's not a verifiable defect strictly from the shown changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: invalidate_upsampling_cache is exported and documented as needing to be called on allowlist config changes, but no code calls it, so cache invalidation is never triggered

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `invalidate_upsampling_cache(...)` in `src/sentry/api/helpers/error_upsampling.py` and documents that it “should be called when the allowlist configuration changes,” but there is no added call site in this PR diff that invokes it. adjudication_records.issue_text: Caching of eligibility uses only org + project_ids as key while eligibility logic depends on dataset/request query split across cache boundary; future conditions added to is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects will be incorrectly cached across queries

adjudication.rationale: In `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects`, the cached value is explicitly only the allowlist check (`is_eligible = _are_all_projects_error_upsampled(...)`), keyed by `organization.id` + `project_ids`. The “future conditions added” concern is speculative and not a verifiable issue from this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Under-scoped wiring: upsampling applied only to organization_events_stats endpoint, so counts disagree with every sibling endpoint (issue counts, org events, dashboards) for the same allowlisted error projects

adjudication.rationale: The diff wires error-upsampling only into `src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_events_stats.py` by conditionally transforming `count()` into `upsampled_count()` via `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects(...)` / `transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling(...)`. No similar transformation is added to other endpoints or query paths in this diff. That makes it a concrete scope/consistency concern: for the same allowlisted projects and error query, this endpoint may return upsampled counts while sibling endpoints still return raw counts. The diff alone doesn’t prove this violates a documented correctness requirement, but it is a real, diff-grounded architectural inconsistency risk introduced by the change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: _should_apply_sample_weight_transform re-imports dataset modules locally and compares against them via a hand-maintained parallel list, so adding a dataset requires editing this hidden list or upsampling silently never applies (or incorrectly applies via the catch-all return False)

adjudication.rationale: In `src/sentry/api/helpers/error_upsampling.py`, `_should_apply_sample_weight_transform` does local imports (`from sentry.snuba import discover, errors, transactions`) and then hard-codes behavior via `if dataset == errors: ... elif dataset == transactions: ... elif dataset == discover: ... else: return False`. This means applicability is governed by a manually maintained set of known datasets; any new dataset module passed in (even if it represents error events / has `sample_weight`) will silently fall into the `return False` branch unless this function is updated. That’s a real maintainability/architecture concern created by this change, though not a verifiable immediate correctness bug for the datasets shown in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The sample_weight column is never written anywhere in the diff — no writer, schema change, or backfill exists, so NULL sample_weight rows are silently dropped by sum(), causing undercounting instead of upsampling

adjudication.rationale: The diff does introduce `upsampled_count()` as `sum(sample_weight)` (in `discover.py`) and does not show any code writing a `sample_weight` field. However, from the diff alone you cannot verify that `sample_weight` is not already produced elsewhere (ingestion/Snuba schema), so “no writer/schema/backfill exists” is not provable. Also the claim that NULL `sample_weight` rows are “silently dropped by sum(), causing undercounting” is a mischaracterization: `sum()` aggregates over rows regardless; NULLs affect the aggregate value, not row inclusion. Therefore the finding overreaches beyond what the diff demonstrates.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Substring match on 'event.type:error' misfires on negation (!event.type:error) and quoted text searches, applying sum(sample_weight) to non-error result sets that sum to 0

When dataset is `discover`, `_should_apply_sample_weight_transform` relies on this function, so these false positives can incorrectly enable `transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling` (replacing `count()` with `upsampled_count()` summing `sample_weight`) even when the actual result set is non-error-focused.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Top-events ranking/selection query (raw_groupby, selected_columns, orderby) is not transformed while its timeseries is, so top-N selection uses raw counts but displays upsampled counts

The finding asserts top-N selection uses “raw counts” because `raw_groupby/selected_columns/orderby` aren’t transformed, but `raw_groupby` and `selected_columns` are not aggregation expressions (so there’s nothing to transform), and the diff does not show that `orderby` is based on an untransformed `count()` expression (it comes from `self.get_orderby(request)`, whose implementation is not in the diff). adjudication_records.issue_text: Eligibility cache is keyed on (org, project_ids) but allowlist changes aren't invalidated — invalidate_upsampling_cache has no callers, and the cache stores negative results for 60s, so allowlist additions don't take effect until staleness clears

adjudication.rationale: In `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects`, the allowlist eligibility is cached for 60s via `cache.set(cache_key, is_eligible, 60)`, which includes caching `False` results. The diff also adds `invalidate_upsampling_cache(...)` but there are no callers shown in this PR, so allowlist changes (especially additions) may not take effect until the TTL expires. The module docstring explicitly frames this as an eventual-consistency/performance tradeoff, so it’s not a clear correctness defect, but it is a concrete, diff-grounded design/operational concern and the invalidation hook appears unused.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The transform only matches the exact literal 'count()'; aliased or wrapped forms like 'count() as errors' silently bypass upsampling

adjudication.rationale: `transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling` only transforms when `column.lower().strip() == "count()"`. Any other valid Snuba/Discover expression containing count—e.g. `"count() as errors"` or more complex/wrapped forms—will not match and will be left unchanged, meaning eligible error upsampling queries would still use raw `count()` and return un-upsampled results. adjudication_records.issue_text: The eligibility check (cache round-trip + dataset import chain) runs unconditionally at the top of every stats request, including transactions-only and top-events=0 paths that can never use it

adjudication_records.issue_text: The same 'if upsampling_enabled: final_columns = transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling(query_columns)' block is copy-pasted three times inside one function, risking inconsistent changes across code paths

adjudication_records.issue_text: Cache key uses Python's salted hash(tuple(sorted(...))) which differs across processes, making invalidate_upsampling_cache a cross-process no-op; should use a stable hash like hashlib
matched_golden_ids: Using Python’s built-in hash() to build cache keys is non-deterministic across processes (hash randomization), so keys won’t match across workers and invalidate_upsampling_cache may fail to delete them. Use a deterministic serialization of project_ids for the cache key.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both comments identify that using Python’s built-in (salted) hash for cache keys is non-deterministic across processes, so keys won’t match between workers and cache invalidation can fail. The candidate also suggests using a stable/deterministic alternative (e.g., hashlib), aligning with the golden recommendation for deterministic key construction.

adjudication_records.issue_text: _is_error_focused_query only matches the literal substring 'event.type:error' in the raw query string, so error-focused queries expressed differently get no upsampling and silently undercount

adjudication_records.issue_text: transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling only rewrites the exact 'count()' token, mixing upsampled totals with raw undercounted values for other aggregations in the same response

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling` only rewrites columns whose normalized text equals exactly `"count()"` into `"upsampled_count() as count"`, leaving any other yAxis expressions untouched (e.g., `count_if(...)`, `count_unique(...)`, etc.). In `organization_events_stats._get_event_stats`, when `upsampling_enabled` is true, the full `query_columns` list is passed through this transformer, so a multi-aggregation request can yield a response where `count()` is upsampled but other count-like aggregations remain unweighted. adjudication_records.issue_text: _is_error_focused_query uses substring matching on raw query string, so negated queries like '!event.type:error' incorrectly trigger error upsampling and return inflated counts

adjudication_records.issue_text: invalidate_upsampling_cache is dead code with no callers, so allowlist revocations only propagate after up to 60s of stale cache

adjudication_records.issue_text: _is_error_focused_query's substring match returns True for negated queries like '!event.type:error', misclassifying non-error queries as error-focused and rewriting count() to sum(sample_weight) on data lacking that column; no tests cover negated forms

adjudication.rationale: In `src/sentry/api/helpers/error_upsampling.py`, `_is_error_focused_query` returns `True` via a simple substring check: `if "event.type:error" in query:`. adjudication.rationale: In `organization_events_stats.py::_get_event_stats`, the upsampling column rewrite is applied in multiple branches: (1) inside `if top_events > 0` before `run_top_events_timeseries_query` and `top_events_timeseries`, (2) inside `if use_rpc` before `run_timeseries_query`, and (3) in the final non-RPC path before `timeseries_query` (all via `transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling`). adjudication_records.issue_text: The upsampled_count SnQLFunction registers default_result_type='number' while the count() it replaces uses 'integer', changing API payload types for allowlisted customers, and no test asserts the response value's type (Python equality passes for both 10 and 10.0)

adjudication_records.issue_text: invalidate_upsampling_cache has no test and no caller anywhere in the diff, making it dead code; combined with the 60s cache, allowlist changes take up to 60s to propagate

adjudication.rationale: In `src/sentry/api/helpers/error_upsampling.py`, `invalidate_upsampling_cache(...)` is newly added but there is no reference/call to it anywhere in the provided diff, and the new tests (`tests/sentry/api/helpers/test_error_upsampling.py` and additions in `tests/snuba/api/endpoints/test_organization_events_stats.py`) do not cover it. adjudication_records.issue_text: mock.patch replaces the entire options module rather than just the allowlist lookup, making every options.get call return a project-ID list; a future second lookup would silently get wrong-typed values while tests still pass

adjudication.rationale: In the new tests, `@patch("sentry.api.helpers.error_upsampling.options")` (and the similar `@mock.patch(...)` in endpoint tests) replaces the `options` module reference inside `sentry.api.helpers.error_upsampling` with a mock. adjudication_records.issue_text: sample_weight column is read by the new aggregation but nothing in the diff writes or backfills it, so existing rows return NULL and counts collapse to zero

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `upsampled_count()` which aggregates `sum(sample_weight)` (in `src/sentry/search/events/datasets/discover.py`) and rewrites `count()` to that function for eligible queries (`transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling`). Within this diff, nothing populates or backfills a `sample_weight` field/column; the only related write is `_set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling(...)` which sets `normalized_data["sample_rate"]`, not `sample_weight` (`src/sentry/testutils/factories.py`). adjudication_records.issue_text: Factory populates sample_rate instead of sample_weight, so the field the query path consumes is never produced; no mapping from sample_rate to sample_weight at ingestion

adjudication.rationale: In this diff, the new aggregation `upsampled_count()` is defined as `sum(sample_weight)` (see `src/sentry/search/events/datasets/discover.py`), and the new query-path transformation replaces `count()` with `upsampled_count()` (see `transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling`). adjudication_records.issue_text: Tests assert count == 10 which no production or test path can produce, hiding the NULL-sum defect

adjudication.rationale: The new tests intentionally set `contexts.error_sampling.client_sample_rate` to `0.1` and the diff adds `_set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling()` in `Factories.store_event()` to copy that into `normalized_data["sample_rate"]`. adjudication_records.issue_text: 60-second eligibility cache creates a dual-read window where projects removed from the allowlist still get the sample_weight query since invalidate_upsampling_cache is never called

adjudication.rationale: The new helper `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects` caches allowlist eligibility for 60s (`cache.set(..., 60)`), so if the allowlist option changes, queries can continue using the cached eligibility result until TTL expiry. The diff adds `invalidate_upsampling_cache(...)` but does not show it being called anywhere, so there is no explicit invalidation path in this PR beyond waiting for TTL. Whether this is a "bug" depends on requirements (the docstring even states eventual consistency is acceptable), but the stale-read window and unused invalidation hook are a concrete, diff-grounded concern.

adjudication_records.issue_text: _is_error_focused_query only detects the literal 'event.type:error' string, so discover queries without it read the upsampled column over a mixed backfill boundary, causing inconsistent counts for the same rows

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `_is_error_focused_query` only returns True when the query string contains the literal `event.type:error` (lowercased), but `_should_apply_sample_weight_transform` applies the upsampling transform for the `discover` dataset **only if** `_is_error_focused_query(request)` is True. adjudication_records.issue_text: Historical events in newly allowlisted projects lack sample_weight, so sum(sample_weight) under-reports counts with HTTP 200 — silent partial success with no enforcement that backfill completed before the allowlist option is flipped

adjudication_records.issue_text: _is_error_focused_query uses raw substring matching on the query string, so negated queries like !(event.type:error) and suffixed/quoted contexts are silently misclassified and get upsampled_count() applied incorrectly

adjudication.rationale: In `src/sentry/api/helpers/error_upsampling.py`, `_is_error_focused_query` returns True whenever the raw query string contains the substring `"event.type:error"` (`if "event.type:error" in query:`). adjudication_records.issue_text: Partial transformation: count_unique(...), count() with an existing alias, and derived columns are left untransformed while count() is upsampled in the same response, mixing scales within one payload with no signal to the consumer

adjudication.rationale: The new `transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling()` only transforms columns whose normalized string is exactly `"count()"` (see `column_lower == "count()"`). Any other count-like aggregations (e.g. `count_unique(...)`) or `count()` expressions with an explicit alias/derivation (e.g. `count() as foo`, `count() + 1`) are left unchanged, while a plain `count()` in the same `y_axes` list is transformed to `upsampled_count() as count`. This can produce a single response payload where some series are upsampled and others are not (mixed scales) and can also create alias conflicts (e.g. `count()` becomes `... as count` while another axis might already be `... as count`). This behavior is directly implied by the diff and can lead to incorrect/ambiguous results for consumers.

adjudication_records.issue_text: invalidate_upsampling_cache has no caller anywhere in the diff — dead code — so on allowlist change, the 60s cache is the only consistency mechanism and stale upsampled data persists up to 60 seconds

adjudication.rationale: In this diff, `invalidate_upsampling_cache(...)` is newly added in `src/sentry/api/helpers/error_upsampling.py` but there are no references to it in any of the changed/added files, while eligibility is cached for 60 seconds via `cache.set(..., 60)` in `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects`. The finding’s implication (that allowlist changes will only take effect after TTL unless something calls the invalidator) is grounded in the diff, but whether it’s truly “dead code” repo-wide can’t be verified from the diff alone, and the file comments explicitly describe eventual consistency as acceptable.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Cache key omits dataset/request context, and on cache hits the dataset half of the eligibility decision is re-evaluated while the allowlist half is frozen, producing asymmetric staleness that can flip the transformation on/off within a rollout window

adjudication.rationale: In `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects`, the cache key (`error_upsampling_eligible:{org}:{hash(project_ids)}`) caches only the allowlist result (`_are_all_projects_error_upsampled`) and intentionally re-evaluates `_should_apply_sample_weight_transform(dataset, request)` on every call. This means the final decision is split across cached (allowlist) vs uncached (dataset/request) inputs, so when allowlist state changes the system can serve a stale allowlist decision for up to 60s while still reflecting current dataset/query context. That asymmetry is real and could yield inconsistent on/off behavior across requests during the TTL window (though it’s not clearly a correctness defect given the comment asserting eventual consistency is acceptable).
